item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 142307
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 PM PDT Fri Aug 14 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles east-southeast of Hilo,
Hawaii.

The National Hurricane Center is also issuing advisories on
Tropical Depression Hernan, located well west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form several hundred miles south of
the coast of southern Mexico by the early to middle part of next
week. Some gradual development of this system is possible thereafter
while the system moves westward or west-northwestward well south of
Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

Western Portion of the East Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well to the west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula by the early to middle
part of next week. Gradual development of this system is possible
thereafter while it moves generally westward across the western
portion of the east Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Mahoney/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Hernan Public Advisory Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026 
115 
WTPZ33 KNHC 150233
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Hernan Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP082026
500 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026
 
...CENTER OF HERNAN REFORMS A LITTLE TO THE NORTH...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 PM HST...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.2N 132.9W
ABOUT 1565 MI...2515 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 PM HST (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Hernan 
was located near latitude 16.2 North, longitude 132.9 West. The 
depression is moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h) and this 
motion is expected to continue through early next week. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Slow weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours, and Hernan is 
forecast to become a post-tropical cyclone within the next day or 
so.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 PM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Mahoney/Pasch

item.title: Tropical Depression Hernan Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 500 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026 
379 
WTPZ43 KNHC 150235
TCDEP3
 
Tropical Depression Hernan Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP082026
500 PM HST Fri Aug 14 2026

The center of Tropical Depression Hernan has reformed since the 
previous advisory, with the system now initialized about 30 mi 
north of the previous track. The center reformation is evident on 
geostationary visible satellite imagery and supported by a recent 
Oceansat-3 scatterometer pass. This also positions Hernan closer 
to its active convection, which is limited to a small area in the 
northeast quadrant. Based on the subjective and objective satellite 
classifications, and the aforementioned scatterometer pass which 
sampled the northwestern quadrant, the initial intensity remains at 
30 kt for this advisory.

The initial motion is an uncertain 275/12 kt, and based primarily 
on visible satellite imagery over the past 4 to 6 h. This generally 
westward motion is expected to continue through the forecast period 
as the cyclone is steered by a deep-layer ridge to the north. Due to 
the center reformation, the new track forecast lies about 30 mi 
north of the previous forecast, and closely follows the HCCA and 
TVCN consensus aids. Moderate vertical wind shear and dry air are 
expected to continue to affect Hernan and lead to the system 
degenerating into a post-tropical cyclone by 24 h. The remnant low 
is forecast to continue westward for a few more days thereafter, 
before dissipating by 72 h. This is in agreement with the
deterministic global model guidance.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  15/0300Z 16.2N 132.9W   30 KT  35 MPH
 12H  15/1200Z 16.3N 134.5W   30 KT  35 MPH
 24H  16/0000Z 16.4N 136.6W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 36H  16/1200Z 16.5N 138.6W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 48H  17/0000Z 16.6N 140.8W   25 KT  30 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 60H  17/1200Z 16.7N 142.5W   20 KT  25 MPH...POST-TROP/REMNT LOW
 72H  18/0000Z...DISSIPATED
